title: Prime elements and localization at a multiplicative set
statement: Let $A$ be an integral domain, let $P$ be a set of prime elements of $A$, and let $S\subseteq A$ be the multiplicative subset of all finite products of elements of $P$ (the empty product $1$ included). Let $S^{-1}A$ be the localization [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] and let $x\in A$ be irreducible. Then $x$ is a prime element of $A$ if and only if its image in $S^{-1}A$ is a prime element or a unit of $S^{-1}A$.

proof.text: Set S = Submonoid.closure P and let f : A → S⁻¹A be the localization map of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Every generator is nonzero by primality, so closure_le puts S inside the non-zero-divisors and IsLocalization.injective gives injectivity of f. If x is prime, split on whether f(x) is a unit. In the nonunit case f(x) is nonzero by injectivity, and Mathlib Submonoid.LocalizationMap.map_prime proves f(x) prime by clearing denominators and applying primality in A. This proves the forward implication without forming a quotient ring.

source.place: Tag 0AFU, proof of clause (2), third and fourth paragraphs: 'For each $i$ either $p_i$ divides $y$ or $p_i$ divides $x$. In the second case $p_i$ and $x$ are associates (as $x$ is irreducible)', written as an induction on the number of prime factors of $s$

proof.text: For the converse, suppose for contradiction that x is not prime. Prove by Submonoid.closure_induction on s ∈ S that, for every y ∈ A, x ∣ s*y implies x ∣ y. For a generator p, Mathlib Prime.left_dvd_or_dvd_right_of_dvd_mul gives p ∣ x or x ∣ y. The former makes p and x associated by their irreducibility, so x is prime, a contradiction. The base s = 1 is immediate. For a product a*b, apply the induction hypothesis first for a to x ∣ a*(b*y), then for b to x ∣ b*y. This handles repeated prime factors as well.

source.place: Tag 0AFU, proof of clause (2), second paragraph (forward implication)

proof.text: Mathlib Submonoid.LocalizationMap.map_dvd_map, the fraction-clearing divisibility criterion for [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], says f(x) ∣ f(a) iff x ∣ s*a for some s ∈ S. Combining it with the preceding closure induction shows that f(x) ∣ f(a) implies x ∣ a. If f(x) is prime and x ∣ a*b, map the divisibility into the localization, apply primality there, and descend the resulting divisibility of f(a) or f(b). Together with hx.ne_zero and hx.not_isUnit this proves x prime, contradicting the assumption.

source.place: Tag 0AFU, proof of clause (2), third paragraph (unit implication)

proof.text: If f(x) is a unit, it divides f(1). Descending divisibility gives x ∣ 1, so x is a unit by isUnit_of_dvd_one, contradicting irreducibility. The two cases exhaust the hypothesis and prove the converse.
